brief.situation: Corvid Media is a healthy, high-engagement account (40 seats, 92% weekly active, NPS 61) with a confirmed base renewal on 1 December 2026, but a $38k ARR Audience Insights expansion plus 25-seat extension has been deferred — not declined — due to a company-wide finance freeze tied to an internal reorg expected to settle by October. The core risk is not churn but momentum loss: the 102-day window between now and renewal overlaps almost exactly with the reorg resolution, making October the critical re-engagement inflection point. A secondary internal gap exists between editorial team enthusiasm and formal product roadmap communication that could quietly erode advocacy if left unmanaged.

leverage_points.what: Send Marcus a brief, value-forward note referencing the July 22 review — acknowledge the October timeline, confirm you will return then with a refined Audience Insights business case, and ask one question about how the reorg is shaping priorities so you arrive prepared.

leverage_points.what: Build a quantified Audience Insights ROI brief tailored to Corvid Media's editorial use case — use the '92% weekly active / morning read' anchor to frame how the module extends existing workflow to the sales team, with a concrete revenue or efficiency metric.
leverage_points.why: The expansion was deferred on budget grounds, not value doubt. When the freeze lifts, Marcus will need internal justification to finance. A ready-made business case lowers his friction and positions you as the one who did the homework.

leverage_points.what: Schedule an October follow-up meeting with Marcus (and ideally one editorial-side advocate) to formally reopen the Audience Insights and 25-seat expansion proposal, with budget unlock confirmation as the qualifying trigger.
leverage_points.why: The reorg is expected to settle by October, and renewal lands December 1. The expansion window is narrow — any slip past October risks compressing the sales cycle into renewal negotiations, weakening your leverage and theirs to act independently.

brief.do_this_today: Draft and send a short, professional email to Marcus Whitfield referencing the July 22 annual review by name, confirming you have the October check-in on your calendar, and asking one forward-looking question — e.g., 'As the reorg progresses, are the priorities around audience analytics shifting at all, or staying consistent with what we discussed?' This keeps the relationship warm without pressuring a frozen budget.

contact_persona.comm_style: Direct and boundary-setting — his July response ('Not this quarter. Come back in October.') is decisive and minimal, no hedging or over-explanation. He communicates in clear, short statements and respects the same in return.
contact_persona.decision_style: Process-driven and constraint-aware: he defers to organizational process (finance freeze, reorg timeline) before personal preference. He does not block on value skepticism — he blocks on structural readiness. Once constraints lift, expect a relatively fast decision.
contact_persona.what_they_say_vs_mean: Says 'not this quarter, come back in October' — means 'I want this but I cannot move it through finance right now; hold the relationship and return with timing.' The deferral is a soft yes, not a soft no.
contact_persona.approach_recommendation: Match his directness — don't over-nurture or flood with touchpoints. One well-timed, well-prepared October pitch with a clean business case will land far better than multiple check-ins. When you do reach out, lead with his constraint (budget readiness) not your product. Frame the October meeting as completing the conversation he started, not reopening a rejected proposal.

secondary_contacts.note: The editorial team are the power users — they coined 'the morning read' and represent the strongest internal advocacy. Identifying and engaging this person before October could generate bottom-up momentum that supports Marcus's internal approval process.

The finance freeze is the actual blocker; understanding who owns the unfreeze decision and whether the reorg has a known end-date would sharpen October timing. Marcus may need air cover from this stakeholder to approve expansion.
